questions.q: What does 'dissipated energy' generally refer to in a physical system?
a: Energy that spreads out into the surroundings and becomes less useful
Energy that is safely stored in a battery for later use
Energy that converts into heavy mass

questions.q: Which term describes a system where no energy enters or leaves the system from outside?
Why is it impossible to build a 100 percent efficient machine that runs forever without adding more energy?
a: Because gravity stops working over time
Because friction and air resistance always dissipate some energy as thermal energy
Because energy is created too quickly

questions.q: How is energy efficiency usually calculated?
a: Total energy input divided by useful energy output
Useful energy output multiplied by total input
Useful energy output divided by total energy input multiplied by 100 percent

questions.q: What happens to the wasted energy produced by a car engine during a journey?
a: It dissipates into the surrounding air and road as thermal energy and sound.
It gets stored safely in the tires.
It disappears from the universe entirely.

questions.q: Which of the following actions helps reduce unwanted energy dissipation through friction in a bicycle chain?
a: Using rough sandpaper on the chain

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of adding thermal insulation (like loft insulation or double glazing) to a house?
a: To reduce the rate of thermal energy transfer to the cold outside environment

Why do moving mechanical parts in machinery get hot during operation?
a: Friction between the parts dissipates mechanical energy into thermal energy.

questions.q: Which material property makes a good thermal insulator for keeping houses warm?
a: High density and solid metal structure
Trapped pockets of air or low thermal conductivity

questions.q: What does the principle of conservation of energy state about total energy?
a: Total energy decreases as time passes.
Total energy in a closed system remains constant.
Total energy can be destroyed easily.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about energy efficiency is correct?
a: Efficiency has no units and is expressed as a ratio or percentage.
Efficiency depends only on the color of the device.

questions.q: How does double glazing reduce thermal energy transfer through windows in winter?
a: The trapped layer of air or gas between the two glass panes acts as a poor thermal conductor.
It lets more light pass through.

questions.q: What happens to the temperature of the surroundings as more energy is dissipated across various appliances?
a: It increases slightly as thermal energy spreads out.

questions.q: Why do engineers streamline cars and trains?
a: To increase the mass of the vehicle
To reduce air resistance and minimize wasted energy due to drag

questions.q: Which of the following energy transfers represents a strictly wasted output for a computer processor?
a: Releasing heat into the computer case from the microchip

questions.q: What does a Sankey diagram visually display for a given machine or process?
a: Energy inputs, useful outputs, and wasted energy outputs
The wiring layout of an electric circuit

a: A thermal store spread so widely it can no longer easily do useful work

questions.q: Why do factory boilers often have layers of lagging or fiberglass insulation wrapped around them?
a: To reduce unwanted thermal energy transfer to the room

Total output energy (useful plus wasted) equals total input energy.
There is no relationship between input and output.

questions.q: What is the primary reason an old incandescent light bulb feels very hot after being on?
a: Most of the electrical energy input is dissipated as thermal energy rather than light.

questions.q: Which of the following represents a practical application of reducing energy waste in transport?
a: Adding heavy steel plates to cars

questions.q: What feature on a Sankey diagram indicates that energy has been conserved overall?
a: The total width of the input arrows equals the combined total width of the output arrows.
The diagram forms a closed circle.

questions.q: Why do sports clothing manufacturers use breathable, moisture-wicking fabrics for runners?
a: To trap all thermal energy permanently
To help regulate body temperature by allowing sweat and thermal energy to transfer away efficiently
